entries.title: EU herbal monograph: chamomile flower (Matricariae flos; EMA name Matricaria recutita)
entries.finding: The EU herbal medicines committee (HMPC) accepts chamomile flower medicines for minor stomach and gut complaints such as bloating and mild spasms, symptoms of the common cold, minor mouth and throat inflammation, and minor skin inflammation and wounds. This rests on long-standing traditional use, and a doctor should be consulted if symptoms last more than a week.
entries.limitations: The committee found the clinical-trial evidence insufficient: the studies it reviewed did not compare chamomile with another treatment. The EU summary also states that it is not practical advice on how to use these medicines.
entries.preparation: Comminuted flowers (herbal tea, infusions) and dry or liquid extracts, including ointments and bath additives
entries.design: Expert committee (HMPC) assessment of long-standing (traditional) use and the available studies
entries.safetyNote: Allergic reactions, sometimes severe, have been reported when liquid chamomile preparations touched the lining of the mouth. The EU summary says these medicines must not be used by people allergic to chamomile or other plants of the daisy family (Asteraceae), that people with severe heart and circulation problems should not take full baths with it, and that people with open wounds, extensive skin damage, acute skin disease, high fever or severe infections should not take full or partial baths with it.
